title: Pulp Fiction
events_chronological: In 1972 a returning POW, Captain Koons, delivers to young Butch Coolidge the gold watch his father hid through years of captivity.
Hitmen Vincent Vega and Jules Winnfield drive across Los Angeles debating Amsterdam, hash bars and the Quarter Pounder.
Waiting in the corridor outside their target's apartment, Vincent and Jules argue over whether a foot massage is worth killing a man for.
Jules recites Ezekiel 25:17 and the pair shoot Brett for double-crossing Marsellus Wallace, recovering the briefcase.
A fourth man hidden in the bathroom empties a revolver at Jules and Vincent without hitting either, which Jules calls divine intervention.
In the car afterwards Vincent's gun goes off and blows the head off their passenger Marvin.
Jules parks the bloodied car at his friend Jimmie's house, where the fixer Winston Wolfe directs the cleanup and gives the men fresh clothes.
Over breakfast in a coffee shop, small-time robbers Pumpkin and Honey Bunny decide on the spot to hold up the diner they are sitting in.
Jules talks Pumpkin down mid-robbery, hands over his own wallet, keeps the briefcase and lets the couple walk out.
Vincent and Jules deliver the briefcase to Marsellus at his bar, where Marsellus is paying the ageing boxer Butch to take a dive in the fifth.
Vincent buys heroin from his dealer Lance and shoots up before his night out.
Vincent takes Marsellus's wife Mia to Jack Rabbit Slim's, where they win the twist contest.
Mia snorts Vincent's heroin, overdoses, and is revived by an adrenaline shot to the heart on Lance's living-room floor.
Butch double-crosses Marsellus, wins the fight and kills his opponent in the ring, then escapes in a taxi.
Hiding in a motel with Fabienne, Butch discovers she has left his father's gold watch behind in his apartment.
Butch returns for the watch and shoots Vincent dead with a submachine gun left on the kitchen counter.
Butch and Marsellus collide in the street, crash, and are taken prisoner in the basement of Maynard's pawnshop.
Butch breaks free, comes back with a katana while Zed is raping Marsellus, and Marsellus declares them square on condition Butch leaves town.
Butch collects Fabienne and rides out of Los Angeles on Zed's chopper.
syuzhet_notes: Told-order bullet 1 is a prologue that is chronologically simultaneous with the film's final bullet - the same diner robbery, seen before and after. Bullet 9 (Captain Koons and the watch) is a childhood flashback arriving inside Butch's dream. Told-order bullets 16-19 loop back to the morning of bullets 2-4, so the film's last chapter precedes most of what came before it, and Vincent appears alive in it after being killed in bullet 12.
fabula_notes: The gap between the diner robbery and the briefcase delivery at the bar is implied only by Jules and Vincent's change into Jimmie's shorts and T-shirts. Captain Koons's monologue is heard inside a dream, so the 1972 scene is recalled rather than dramatised as present action.
